I joined back in 2011 (I think?) and had a couple of accounts. I had my fun there while it lasted, but eventually some small pesky elements began to come into my view, and then into my circles.

The first thing, naturally, was the groupthink mentality. If you opposed this mentality in any way, you usually got downvoted to oblivion, regardless of the fact that you had something beneficial to add to the discussion. Occasionally, you were banned.

Next came SRS and their horseshit. This was the big motivator, really. I noticed the complete impunity they had while harassing, and in some cases doxxing, other users. I noticed how they'd invade other boards by weaseling their way into moderator positions, and then everything would change for the worse. Tone policing. Thought policing. All the prefixes and politically correct language. Check your privilege. Blah blah fucking blah. Nothing at all can make these people happy because they're intent on being miserable, so they'll go out of their way to make you miserable, too. They're not the only SJW microcosm out there, but they were bad enough to gain notoriety throughout Reddit. Fitting for a group of people who talk endless amounts of shit about 4chan, yet adopt 4chan's strategies.

Then I noticed the "power moderators" who put themselves in charge of a bafflingly large amount of subreddits. The last one I noticed was in charge of over 180. While innocuous at first thought, I began to realize that this gives one person an inordinate amount of influence over flow and content. It also allows one to essentially act as the Thought Police. (See: SRS).

Then there was Reddit Enhancement Suite, which eventually started asking for permissions that I wasn't comfortable giving.

After that was the cabal exposure thanks to Kamen. Strike one was how the people he was accusing weren't really refuting what he was saying, but rather, trying desperately to destroy his credibility. "Listen to how crazy he sounds", I read from one accused powermod. Strike two was how Kamen, and all the other mod accounts, were shadowbanned instantly upon his announcement, and his subreddit was subsequently deleted, though not before SRS made an attempt to claim it and add it to the myriad other subreddits they've already invaded. And Reddit, funny enough, says it doesn't censor people.

Strike three, the final nail in the coffin, was a former /r/games moderator who spilled a lot of information about the inner workings of Reddit. How much power the admins really have. How they can see everything, from hidden and deleted posts to modmail and private messages. How they'll essentially end all communication with you (which is necessary to get something done with your subreddit) if they don't like you. How, if they really want to get rid of you, they'll make up an excuse off the top of their head and ban you. It makes sense, after all, it's their system, their playground, even if they were advertising it as a system based on rules. However, this was unsettling: they shadowbanned Kamen in minutes, but no one from SRS after years of dox, harassment, hostility, brigading, and general interference in other subreddits. The admins can see all the PMs, all the encouragement, all the bullshit and do nothing to stop it, but as soon as one user cries foul, the reaction is immediate. Fuck that. Fuck Reddit. Open forum, my ass.

A place free of censors is not that great when its userbase is forced to self-censor in fear of official (or unofficial) reprisal. The many instances in which users have failed to "watch their tone" and faced consequences is, in essence, why I'm here. I just hope this place goes in a better direction than the shithole I came from.
